docs.description: The columns: [{key, label?, width?, align?, sortable?}]. width is a CSS grid track (a number is px; default minmax(6rem, 1fr)); align is start, center or end. A row's value for a key is a scalar or a cell object {value, text?, suffix?, href?, tone?}.

The rows at hand, objects keyed by column: all of them, or the window the server sent, starting at row offset. A value is a scalar, or a cell object {value, text, suffix, href, tone}: text replaces the formatted value, suffix follows it muted, href (http, https or mailto) makes it a link, tone (info, success, warning, danger, neutral) a badge. value is the sort key. Nothing is rendered as HTML.
Index of the first row in rows.
How many rows there are (at least offset plus the rows given).
The field that identifies a row, for the selection and sb-row-activate.
The height of every row, in px: fixed, so the scroll position tells which rows are in view.
How much to keep ready above and below the view, in px of rows.

The order the rows are in: {key, dir: "asc" | "desc"}. The server sends it with the rows. When the table holds every row (offset 0, no more than total), a header click sorts them here too; otherwise it asks for the order (sb-sort). A new sort from the server wins.
Rows are on their way (bind it to data-indicator): the table is aria-busy.
How many rows can be selected.
The selection: a JSON array of row keys. A new list from the server replaces it; the live value is the selected property.
Server-confirmed selection: :state(pending) while the local selection differs from the server's selected attribute (see revert()).
Name reported in sb-change, sb-columns and sb-export (e.g. the field of a command).

View state: the keys of the columns not shown, as a JSON array. A changed list from the server wins; the same list again keeps the user's choice. The live list is the hiddenColumns property. At least one column always shows.
Show a Columns button in the toolbar, with a menu that shows and hides columns (sb-columns).
The Columns button's text, and the accessible name of its menu.

slots.name: toolbar
slots.description: Your own controls (e.g. export buttons), in a toolbar above the table, before the Columns button.

events.name: sb-window
events.description: The view needs rows the table doesn't have (also on connect and on resize): detail { offset, count }, plus key and dir of the order to send them in. Answer with rows from that offset, offset and total.

events.name: sb-sort
events.description: A sortable header was clicked. detail: { key, dir }, plus the window to answer with (offset 0, count). Answer with those rows in that order, and the new sort; a table that holds every row has sorted them already.

events.name: sb-row-activate
events.description: Enter or a double click on a row (not on a link in it). detail: { key }.

events.name: sb-cell-activate
events.description: A click or middle click on a link in a cell, or Enter on its cell. detail: { key, column, value, href }. Cancelable: preventDefault() stops the navigation, for an in-page action instead.

events.name: sb-change
events.description: The selection changed. detail: { name, value } (an array of row keys): ready for a command.

events.name: sb-export
events.description: requestExport(format) was called. detail: { name, format, sort: { key, dir }, columns, selected }: the order on screen, the keys of the shown columns in order, and the local selection. The page asks the server for the file; the table never builds one.

events.name: sb-columns
events.description: The user showed or hid a column in the column picker. detail: { name, hidden } (the keys of every hidden column). View state: not emitted for a change the server made or a property write.
